newsitem.title: USA: Whirlpool posts sharply higher profits.
newsitem.headline: Whirlpool posts sharply higher profits.

text.p: Whirlpool Corp., the nation's biggest maker of home appliances, Tuesday reported a sharp rebound in earnings for the latest quarter, thanks to "outstanding" gains in North American and Latin American markets.
But the strong fourth-quarter results were not enough to reverse a poor performance for the balance of the year.

The Benton Harbor, Mich.-based company said its profits more than doubled to $45 million, or 60 cents a share, in the fourth quarter, compared with year-earlier earnings of $18 million, or 25 cents a share. Revenues were flat at $2.1 billion.

Whirlpool has been struggling for the past year, partly due to weak results in Europe. For all of 1996, it reported profits of $156 million, equal to $2.08 a share, down from year-earlier earnings of $209 million, or $2.80 a share. Revenues for the year were $8.69 billion, up from $8.34 billion.
"Bottom-line financial results were disappointing," said Chairman and Chief Executive David Whitwam.
"The operating performances of our North American and Latin American appliance groups in 1996 were outstanding, and we expect further solid results from them this year," he said.

"We believe that our European business is on a trend of gradual improvement that will carry through 1997, and we anticipate better results from Whirlpool Asia as our volumes in that important market continue to grow," Whitwam said.
The company said its North American operating results were up 17 percent in the fourth quarter, and the European operation was profitable, extending a recovery that started in the second-quarter.
Latin American earnings were up 30 percent in the quarter.
Whirlpool's stock was up 62.5 cents at $50.125 in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
